purpose: Measure whether contamination detector separability is concealed by later optimization while benchmark performance inflation remains.

literature_anchor.title: On the Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models
reported_findings: Several reference-free detectors identify SFT contamination before RL; the paper reports mean AUROC around 73.42% across six benchmarks, and LiRA around 89.13% where its reference assumptions hold.
After clean GRPO, detector AUROC systematically decreases; up to 156 additional GRPO steps are reported.
The contaminated model retains approximately 7.14 percentage points of average pass@1 inflation across six benchmarks after clean GRPO.
A final CoT SFT contamination stage on advanced LRMs leaves several reasoning and coding detector results near chance.
The paper evaluates LiveCodeBench v2 and MMLU-Pro beyond mathematics.
literature_anchor.interpretation: Paper-reported results are replication targets, not universal laws or Symthaea results.

statistical_design.calibration_threshold: For each detector and checkpoint, choose the conservative score threshold from calibration non-members at the preregistered target FPR; evaluate TPR/FPR only on the held-out test split.
statistical_design.threshold_ties: Strict score > threshold; tied items at threshold are not flagged, making the empirical calibration false-positive count no greater than the allowed integer budget.
statistical_design.confidence_intervals: Wilson 95% intervals for held-out TPR/FPR; Student-t 95% intervals across independent model-pair replicates for aggregate retention and inflation measures.
statistical_design.multiplicity: Not adjusted in v1; all method × stage × domain comparisons must be treated as exploratory unless a separate preregistered multiplicity plan is supplied.
statistical_design.power: Final replicate and item counts are selected by preregistered power simulation using pair-level variance, detector heterogeneity and domain interactions.

measures.auroc: Rank-based, tie-corrected AUROC on held-out test examples.
measures.auprc: Average precision by grouped score thresholds on held-out test examples.
measures.fixed_fpr: TPR and FPR at the calibration-selected threshold; Wilson intervals are reported.
measures.member_performance_inflation: Treatment checkpoint member accuracy minus its matched clean-control checkpoint member accuracy, on the same held-out member-labeled items.
measures.member_inflation_retention: 1000 * member_inflation_after / member_inflation_before, only defined when before inflation is positive.
measures.nonmember_generalization_delta: Treatment checkpoint non-member accuracy minus matched clean-control non-member accuracy.
measures.concealment_gap: member_inflation_retention - detector_signal_retention; report the two components separately and never rank by gap alone.

detector_panel: likelihood/loss/Max-K% and reference-based LiRA where assumptions are satisfied
Self-Critique paper-faithful top-K and separately full-vocabulary modes
lexical, syntactic, embedding and benchmark-audit controls

qualification_targets.claim_rule: A detector is robust only to the intervention families and domains actually tested. AUC or TPR improvement before concealment does not imply lifecycle robustness.

claim_ceiling: Model pair receipts and digests are declared consistency evidence until an independent signer/trust-root and execution-custody verifier is present.
The benchmark can show reduced detectability after an intervention; it cannot infer developer intent.
Preserved task performance is not proof of membership or generalization unless the intervention and item labels are authenticated.
No multiplicity-adjusted confirmatory claims are emitted in v1.
Wilson intervals are not exact Clopper-Pearson intervals.
No universal detector claim or SOTA superiority is established by synthetic fixtures.
